notes.meaning: The prophet calls on the people of Israel to return all the way back to the Lord, who is still their God. Their terrible ruin was not caused by bad luck or enemy armies, but by their own persistent sin. Even after many warnings of judgment, God still leaves the door wide open for them to turn around and be restored.

God kindly tells the people the very words they should pray when coming back to Him. He asks for honest, heartfelt confession of sin rather than mere animal sacrifices. When God pardons their guilt and shows His favor, His people respond with thankful praise, which is the true fruit of their lips.

Real repentance requires casting away every false source of rescue. Israel promises never again to rely on political deals with Assyria, war horses from Egypt, or handmade idols that cannot speak. They place themselves in God's hands like helpless orphans, knowing that only He has pity on the needy.

God answers their plea by promising to cure their unfaithfulness and heal the damage caused by wandering away from Him. He promises to love them freely, out of His own pure generosity and not because they earned it. Because they have returned to Him with their whole heart, His holy anger is completely turned away.

God compares His life-giving presence to the heavy morning dew that revives parched ground in a hot country. Under His blessing, Israel will blossom quickly and beautifully like an open lily. At the same time, their spiritual life will sink deep, unshakeable roots like the massive cedar trees of Lebanon.

The picture of growth continues as Israel spreads out healthy new branches in every direction. The nation will share the lasting beauty and rich value of an evergreen olive tree. Their life and worship will give off a pleasing, refreshing scent like the cedar forests and spices of the Lebanon mountains.

Those who find shelter under the shade of restored Israel will be revived and protected. They will spring up like fresh grain after a harvest and flourish like a fruitful grape arbor. Their good name and reputation will be as delightful and well regarded as the famous wine of Lebanon.

Ephraim is changed so deeply by God's kindness that the people gladly abandon every worthless idol forever. The Lord reminds them that He is the one who hears their cries and watches over them day and night. Like an evergreen cypress tree, He gives them shade and shelter, and every good fruit in their lives comes entirely from Him.

Hosea finishes his entire book by urging wise and thoughtful people to take these lessons to heart. Everything God does and commands is perfectly right, fair, and good. The righteous walk safely along His paths, but rebellious people trip and fall over the very truths meant to save them.
